To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The first nucleosome adjacent to a DSB is rapidly repositioned in G1 arrested cells, and that the loss of nucleosome organization is dependent upon the MRX complex.
The first nucleosome adjacent to a double strand break is repositioned in a dynamic process that is distinct from the broader loss of chromatic organization that is dependent on end processing.

1) the loss of chromatin structure following a DSB is dynamic, 2) the first nucleosome flanking the DSB is repositioned in a manner independent of end processing, 3) this repositioning is followed by a broad loss of chromatic structure, and 4) the re establishment of the original chromatin structure following NHEJ mediated DSB repair in G1 cells is independent of DNA replication.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of chromatin in DSB repair and how the repair process impacts the epigenome.
the role of epigentic processes in the recognition of and response to DSBs.
how epigenetic processes are involved in the recognition, repair and reestablishment of the chromatin organization of DNA damage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our work demonstrates a novel role for the MRX end processing complex in the early repositioning of nucleosomes adjacent to a DSB and that this repositioning event is independent of the MRN end processing complex.
in the absence of replication, the local chromatin structure surrounding a DSB is preserved through NHEJ mediated DSB repair.
local chromatin dynamics and eviction following DSB are reversible by Nhej mediated repair in the absense of DNA replication.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in G1 arrested cells, DSBs can be repaired by a DNA replication independent NHEJ pathway that does not require end resection, and that preserves the epigenetic landscape of the pre lesion locus.
the local remodeling of nucleosomes adjacent to a DSB is a dynamic process, that occurs in a replication independent manner.
the local nucleosome dynamics that are observed following a DSB in the absence of end resection are reversible and that this process is dependent on the NHEJ mediated pathway of DSB repair.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the chromatin landscape is dynamic following a DSB.
nucleosome eviction and repositioning occur in a stepwise manner and that the early reorganization of chromatin structure following a DSB is a DNA end processing independent process.
the epigenetic landscape of the DSB is dynamic.
